challenge.alternative: A swizzle eliminates bank conflicts by construction, regardless of consumer access.
challenge.check: Apply the documented bank mapping to different warp address sets and include same-word/broadcast cases.
challenge.outcome: Conflicts are properties of the concrete request; the page defines that dependency and limits swizzle benefit to a target access pattern.

claims.claim: Shared memory maps successive 32-bit words to 32 banks, conflicts serialize different-word same-bank accesses within a warp request, and a swizzle may reduce but cannot universally eliminate conflicts.

evidence.observation: The guide defines 32 banks, successive 32-bit-word mapping, conflict serialization, and same-word/broadcast exceptions.

challenge.alternative: 128B is the only legal Blackwell mapping, and a tensor-map enumerator alone determines correctness.
challenge.check: Compare TMA enum mappings, encoder constraints, and tcgen05 descriptor layout values.
challenge.outcome: Both APIs expose multiple modes and independent constraints, while the producer destination and consumer addressing must denote the same physical layout; the page lists exact common encodings.

claims.claim: A TMA-to-tcgen05 tile requires consistent tensor-map, base/alignment, and consumer-descriptor mappings; CUDA 13 defines the listed TMA chunk spans and PTX 9.0 defines legal no/32B/64B/128B tcgen05 modes with exact layout-field values and combination-specific constraints.

evidence.observation: The API lists NONE, 32B/64B/128B 16B-chunk mappings and 128B atom variants, plus datatype/interleave/inner-box restrictions.

evidence.locator: tcgen05 shared-memory descriptor and valid combinations
evidence.observation: PTX defines the descriptor fields, layout values, invalid values, and type/major/shape constraints quoted by the page.

challenge.alternative: Swizzle<3,4,3> means three base bits, four mask bits, and can be applied from row indices without base alignment.
challenge.check: Evaluate the CUTLASS template masks and compare layout versus pointer swizzling.
challenge.outcome: The template source defines the opposite parameter meanings, yields address bits 7:9 into 4:6, and explicitly distinguishes position-dependent hardware pointers; the page matches.

claims.claim: CUTLASS Swizzle<BBits,MBase,SShift> uses mask width, invariant low bits, and field distance respectively; Swizzle<3,4,3> maps address bits 7:9 into 4:6, with equivalence to a logical row formula dependent on stride, byte units, composition, and base alignment.

evidence.observation: The header defines parameter meanings, mask positions, and XOR application exactly as summarized.
CUTLASS states that hardware chose position-dependent swizzles and distinguishes swizzle_ptr from composed swizzle_layout.

challenge.alternative: Supplying CU_TENSOR_MAP_SWIZZLE_128B is sufficient, and any mismatch always appears as a runtime error.
challenge.check: Enumerate every encoder input/constraint and distinguish invalid encoding from a legal but logically inconsistent consumer.
challenge.outcome: The driver validates encoder contracts through CUresult, while consumer semantics are separate; the checklist and two failure classes are correctly separated.

claims.claim: A reproducible tiled tensor map must validate alignment, rank-specific dimensions/strides, box and element strides, mode constraints, CUresult, and the matching consumer mapping; successful encoding alone does not validate logical MMA output.

evidence.locator: cuTensorMapEncodeTiled parameters, return values, and constraints
evidence.observation: The archived API defines output/base alignment, rank-sized arrays, rank-minus-one byte strides, box/element constraints, swizzle restrictions, and CUresult failures.
The consumer descriptor independently supplies base, leading/stride dimensions, offset, major mode, and swizzle layout.

challenge.alternative: The 2.75x result isolates bank-conflict removal by 128B swizzling.
challenge.check: Diff the tutorial's v1b/v2b encoder, TMA issuance, and descriptors and read the author's causal discussion.
challenge.outcome: The inner TMA width and loop structure change together with swizzle/descriptor mode, and the author explicitly proposes TMA efficiency as an alternative; the page reports a combined treatment.

claims.claim: The pinned tutorial's B200 4096-cube 3D TMA path reports 252.81 TFLOP/s for 16B/no-swizzle and 695.43 for 128B/128B-swizzle, approximately 2.75x and 46% of its cuBLAS result, without isolating bank-conflict or swizzle causality.

evidence.locator: 128-byte global load and swizzling, v1/v2 diff, benchmark, and remarks
evidence.observation: The first-party tutorial supplies the exact values, simultaneous 16B-to-128B TMA and swizzle changes, lack of ncu access, and alternative wider-load explanation.

challenge.alternative: A zero conflict counter or successful tensor-map encode is sufficient to select and validate a swizzle.
challenge.check: Separate encoding validity, output permutation correctness, per-access wavefronts, and end-to-end timing.
challenge.outcome: Each oracle discriminates a different failure mode, and the procedure controls producer/consumer pairs, correctness, profiler-version metric discovery, resources, and timing.

claims.claim: Swizzle verification requires controlled matched-layout variants, explicit encoder and output checks, tool-discovered shared-memory request/wavefront/conflict metrics, end-to-end timing, and recorded environment rather than one counter or architecture heuristic.

evidence.locator: Metrics Examples and Shared Memory table
evidence.observation: Nsight Compute documents metric discovery/naming, l1tex bank-conflict aggregates, and requests/wavefronts/conflicts as distinct shared-memory observations.
The producer and consumer interfaces have separate validity and layout requirements, supporting independent encoding and numerical checks.

residual_risk: No GPU experiment was available. The page intentionally requires per-consumer correctness and profiler comparison because legal mappings do not imply conflict-free or faster execution.
scope: All 39 current body units, exact enum/descriptor values, CUTLASS semantics, performance provenance, validation workflow, and frontmatter claim were checked.
